name: Partnachklamm Gorge
access: Walk from the Olympic ski stadium in Garmisch-Partenkirchen
access_note: Entry €10; the path past the gorge to Vordergraseck is closed 21 Sep – 20 Nov 2026 for construction.
trending_reason: A 700 m long, 80 m deep gorge that freezes into icicle curtains in winter
blurb: A railed path and tunnels through a 700 m long, 80 m deep limestone gorge, roaring with meltwater in spring and hung with icicles in winter.
description: A narrow gorge 700 m long and up to 80 m deep, carved by the Partnach just outside Garmisch-Partenkirchen. A railed path and tunnels lead through it beside the roaring water, and in winter the walls hang with icicles. Walk in from the Olympic ski stadium; it is open all year (admission) and can be extended up to Graseck or towards the Reintal.

name: Höllentalklamm Loop
access: Zugspitzbahn or car to Hammersbach (P2 €13 per 12 h)
access_note: Bridges are removed over winter; the gorge reopens around late May.
trending_reason: Wild tunnels and waterfalls at the foot of the Zugspitze, quieter than the Partnachklamm
blurb: Through the dripping tunnels of the Höllentalklamm to the Höllentalangerhütte under the Zugspitze, returning over the airy Stangensteig.
description: A wilder, quieter gorge at the foot of the Zugspitze: tunnels and galleries lead up the Höllentalklamm beside thundering water to the Höllentalangerhütte (1,381 m), with the Zugspitze’s walls closing in above. Return over the airy Stangensteig balcony path to make a loop. The gorge’s bridges are taken down over winter; it reopens around late May.

name: Eibsee Loop
access: Train, bus or car to the Zugspitze cable car valley station
trending_reason: Caribbean-coloured water and islands under the Zugspitze
blurb: An easy loop round a clear, island-studded lake, with the 2,000 m north face of the Zugspitze rising straight above it.
description: An easy loop round the Eibsee, a clear green lake dotted with small islands at the foot of the Zugspitze, whose north face rises 2,000 m straight above the water. The path is mostly flat, through forest and along the shore, with swimming and boat hire in summer. Start at the Zugspitze cable car valley station.

name: Zugspitze via the Höllental
access: Start in Hammersbach; most descend by cable car
access_note: Glacier (Höllentalferner) plus via ferrata: crampons, helmet and harness.
trending_reason: Germany’s highest summit by its most spectacular route
blurb: Germany’s highest summit the hard way: the Höllental gorge, a night at the Höllentalangerhütte, then the Höllentalferner glacier and a long via ferrata to the top.
description: The most spectacular way up Germany’s highest summit (2,962 m): through the Höllentalklamm to the Höllentalangerhütte for the night, then over the “Leiter” and “Brett” ledges, across the Höllentalferner glacier and up a long via ferrata to the top, where the cable car waits. About 2,200 m of ascent; crampons, helmet and via-ferrata kit required, and the gap at the glacier’s top edge can be tricky late in summer.

name: Marienbrücke & Neuschwanstein
access_note: The bridge closes in snow and ice; the Pöllat gorge path was closed through 2024 after storm damage, so check before going.
trending_reason: The fairytale-castle view from the bridge is one of Germany’s most photographed scenes
blurb: Up from Hohenschwangau to the iron Marienbrücke over the Pöllat gorge, for the classic view of Neuschwanstein Castle.
description: The classic view of Neuschwanstein Castle: a walk up from Hohenschwangau to the Marienbrücke, an iron footbridge high above the Pöllat gorge, with the castle on its crag across the void. The bridge gets very busy and closes in snow and ice; the Pöllat gorge path below was closed through 2024 after storm damage, so check before planning a loop.

name: Königssee: St. Bartholomä to the Eiskapelle
access: Electric boat across the Königssee from Schönau to St. Bartholomä
access_note: The ice chapel has collapsed and entering it is prohibited; walk to the viewpoint only.
trending_reason: The onion-domed chapel of St. Bartholomä under the Watzmann east face is the classic Bavarian postcard
blurb: Boat across the fjord-like Königssee to St. Bartholomä, then walk up into the cirque under the huge Watzmann east face to the remains of the Eiskapelle snowfield.
description: Cross the fjord-like Königssee by electric boat to St. Bartholomä, the onion-domed pilgrimage chapel under the Watzmann east face. A forest path then climbs gently into the cirque at the foot of the face to the Eiskapelle, a snowfield fed by avalanches. The ice chapel itself has collapsed and entering is forbidden: enjoy it from the viewpoint and keep clear of the ice.

name: Almbachklamm & Ettenberg
access: Bus 840 from Berchtesgaden, or car to the Kugelmühle
access_note: Closed in winter because of falling ice; small entry fee.
trending_reason: Clear pools and waterfalls in a narrow gorge, up to a pilgrimage church
blurb: Up the Almbachklamm on steps and bridges past green pools to the Theresienklause, then to the Ettenberg pilgrimage church and back down.
description: A short but beautiful gorge near Berchtesgaden: steps, bridges and tunnels lead up the Almbachklamm past clear green pools and waterfalls to the Theresienklause, an old log-driving dam. Climb on to the Ettenberg pilgrimage church for the view of the Untersberg, then return on the Hammerstielweg. Closed in winter because of falling ice.

name: Watzmann Traverse
access: Bus or car to Wimbachbrücke, Ramsau
access_note: Exposed, cabled ridge: a long two-day tour with a night at the Watzmannhaus.
blurb: Over all three Watzmann summits on an exposed, cabled ridge, with a night at the Watzmannhaus and a long descent through the Wimbachgries.
description: Germany’s most famous ridge tour: up to the Watzmannhaus for the night, then over all three summits, Hocheck, Mittelspitze (2,713 m) and Südspitze, on an exposed, cabled ridge with huge drops down the east face to the Königssee. The descent through the Wimbachgries is long and loose. Two long days with about 2,300 m of ascent: for experienced, surefooted mountaineers only.

name: Herzogstand–Heimgarten Ridge
trending_reason: Walchensee and Kochelsee in one view; a favourite day trip from Munich
blurb: From the Herzogstandbahn to the Herzogstand pavilion and along the cabled ridge to the Heimgarten, with Walchensee on one side and Kochelsee on the other.
description: From the Herzogstandbahn above Walchensee a short climb leads to the Herzogstand pavilion (1,731 m), a favourite of King Ludwig II, with Walchensee on one side and Kochelsee on the other. The narrow, partly cabled ridge then continues to the Heimgarten (1,790 m); walk back the same way for the cable car. Surefootedness needed on the ridge, and it is very popular at weekends.

name: Alpspitze Via Ferrata
access: Alpspitzbahn cable car to the Osterfelderkopf
access_note: B-grade via ferrata: helmet and full kit required.
trending_reason: Germany’s classic via ferrata to a pyramid summit above Garmisch
blurb: Steel cables and ladders up the north face of the pyramid-shaped Alpspitze from the Alpspitzbahn, and down the Nordwandsteig.
description: Germany’s classic via ferrata climbs the north face of the pyramid-shaped Alpspitze (2,628 m) above Garmisch-Partenkirchen. From the Alpspitzbahn top station at the Osterfelderkopf, cables and ladders (grade B) lead up the face to the summit cross; descend by the Nordwandsteig for a loop. Helmet and full kit required; the AlpspiX viewing platform by the lift is worth a look.

name: Breitachklamm Gorge
access: Bus from Oberstdorf, or park at P1 Tiefenbach (€5)
access_note: Open daily with last entry at 16:00; online tickets; closures possible in bad weather.
blurb: One of the deepest gorges in Central Europe: a walkway cut into the rock above the roaring Breitach, with frozen waterfalls on the winter walks.
description: One of the deepest gorges in Central Europe, up to 150 m deep, cut by the Breitach near Oberstdorf. A walkway hewn into the rock leads through it above the roaring water, and in winter the frozen waterfalls make it a different world. Open daily with online tickets; named Germany’s natural wonder of 2025.
